The '''Nogi Shrine''' (乃木神社 ''Tōgō-jinja'') was built in 1917 and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] after his death. It is located in [[Kyoto]], [[Japan]].
There, Nogi Maresuke is celebrated as a [[Shinto|shinto]] [[Kami|kami]].

revision.text:
{{Infobox Shinto shrine | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image =Nogi-Shrine-Tokyo-01.jpg | caption = Nogi Shrine | type = | dedication = | founded = | closed = | founder = | priest = | reisai = | honden = | location_map = Japan | coordinates ={{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | address = | phone = | website = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the Meiji period.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1957.<ref name="pamphlet" />
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara, Tochigi]] Prefecture *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō, Saitama]] Prefecture
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}
{{Shinto shrine}}
{{DEFAULTSORT:Nogi Shrine}} [[Category:Shinto shrines in Tokyo]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the Meiji period.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara, Tochigi]] Prefecture *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō, Saitama]] Prefecture
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052 [[Category:Beppo Shrines]]
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the Meiji period.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara, Tochigi]] Prefecture *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō, Saitama]] Prefecture
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

revision.text:
{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
