{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[Nogizaka Station]] on the [[Tokyo Metro]] [[Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[Togo Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[Meiji era|Meiji period]].{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''.{{citation needed|date=April 2013}} There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[Nasushiobara]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[Shimonoseki]], [[Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[Hannō]], [[Saitama Prefecture]]

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[arz:ضريح نوجى]][[sn:commons:Category:Nogi-jinja (Minato, Tokyo)]][[de:Nogi-Schrein]][[en:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[fa:معبد نوگی]][[fr:Nogi-jinja]][[id:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[ja:乃木神社 (東京都港区)]][[zh:乃木神社 (東京都港區)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q3342690]] Wikidata name: Nogi Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:34, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]]. It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[:en:Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''. There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[:en:Nasushiobara|Nasushiobara]], [[:en:Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[:en:Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[:en:Shimonoseki|Shimonoseki]], [[:en:Yamaguchi Prefecture|Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[:en:Hannō|Hannō]], [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[:en:Nogizaka Station|Nogizaka Station]] on the [[:en:Tokyo Metro|Tokyo Metro]] [[:en:Chiyoda Line|Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[:en:Tōgō Shrine|Tōgō Shrine]]

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[arz:ضريح نوجى]][[commons:Category:Nogi-jinja (Minato, Tokyo)]][[de:Nogi-Schrein]][[en:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[fa:معبد نوگی]][[fr:Nogi-jinja]][[id:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[ja:乃木神社 (東京都港区)]][[zh:乃木神社 (東京都港區)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[arz:ضريح نوجى]][[commons:Category:Nogi-jinja (Minato, Tokyo)]][[de:Nogi-Schrein]][[en:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[fa:معبد نوگی]][[fr:Nogi-jinja]][[id:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[ja:乃木神社 (東京都港区)]][[zh:乃木神社 (東京都港區)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[arz:ضريح نوجى]][[sn:commons:Category:Nogi-jinja (Minato, Tokyo)]][[de:Nogi-Schrein]][[en:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[fa:معبد نوگی]][[fr:Nogi-jinja]][[id:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[ja:乃木神社 (東京都港区)]][[zh:乃木神社 (東京都港區)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q3342690]] Wikidata name: Nogi Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:34, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], [[:en:Japan|Japan]].
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji period]]. It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the [[:en:Air raids on Japan|1945 air raids]] on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''. There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*[[:en:Nasushiobara|Nasushiobara]], [[:en:Tochigi Prefecture|Tochigi Prefecture]] *[[:en:Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto]] *[[:en:Shimonoseki|Shimonoseki]], [[:en:Yamaguchi Prefecture|Yamaguchi Prefecture]] *[[:en:Hannō|Hannō]], [[:en:Saitama Prefecture|Saitama Prefecture]]
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from [[:en:Nogizaka Station|Nogizaka Station]] on the [[:en:Tokyo Metro|Tokyo Metro]] [[:en:Chiyoda Line|Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*[[:en:Tōgō Shrine|Tōgō Shrine]]
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

<!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[arz:ضريح نوجى]][[co:commons:Category:Nogi-jinja (Minato, Tokyo)]][[de:Nogi-Schrein]][[en:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[fa:معبد نوگی]][[fr:Nogi-jinja]][[id:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[ja:乃木神社 (東京都港区)]][[zh:乃木神社 (東京都港區)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[arz:ضريح نوجى]][[co:commons:Category:Nogi-jinja (Minato, Tokyo)]][[de:Nogi-Schrein]][[en:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[fa:معبد نوگی]][[fr:Nogi-jinja]][[id:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[ja:乃木神社 (東京都港区)]][[zh:乃木神社 (東京都港區)]] <!--interwikis from wikidata-->[[arz:ضريح نوجى]][[sn:commons:Category:Nogi-jinja (Minato, Tokyo)]][[de:Nogi-Schrein]][[en:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[fa:معبد نوگی]][[fr:Nogi-jinja]][[id:Nogi Shrine (Tokyo)]][[ja:乃木神社 (東京都港区)]][[zh:乃木神社 (東京都港區)]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q3342690]] Wikidata name: Nogi Shrine [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:34, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}. It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the {{ill|Air raids on Japan|en|Air raids on Japan|WD=Q590545|lt=1945 air raids}} on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''. There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*{{ill|Nasushiobara|en|Nasushiobara|WD=Q498027|lt=Nasushiobara}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} *{{ill|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|en|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|WD=Q1197771|lt=Fushimi-ku, Kyoto}} *{{ill|Shimonoseki|en|Shimonoseki|WD=Q203308|lt=Shimonoseki}}, {{ill|Yamaguchi Prefecture|en|Yamaguchi Prefecture|WD=Q127264|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture}} *{{ill|Hannō|en|Hannō|WD=Q850472|lt=Hannō}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from {{ill|Nogizaka Station|en|Nogizaka Station|WD=Q347791|lt=Nogizaka Station}} on the {{ill|Tokyo Metro|en|Tokyo Metro|WD=Q682894|lt=Tokyo Metro}} [[:en:Chiyoda Line|Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*{{ill|Tōgō Shrine|en|Tōgō Shrine|WD=Q1384780|lt=Tōgō Shrine}}
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Tokyo, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} | image = Nogi shrine in Minato Tokyo - September 19 2021 various 01 16 24 157000.jpeg | caption = Nogi Shrine, 2021 | map_type = Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|40|08|N|139|43|41|E|source:kolossus-jawiki|display=title,inline}} | map_relief = | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location = | website = | architecture_style = | festival = | leadership = }} {{nihongo|'''Nogi Shrine'''|乃木神社|Nogi-jinja}} was established on November 1, 1923<ref name="pamphlet">English language pamphlet collected from Shrine on 2015-02-18</ref> and dedicated to General [[Nogi Maresuke]] (63) and his wife [[Nogi Shizuko]] (53) after their death on September 13, 1912. The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan}}.
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period}}. It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the {{ill|Air raids on Japan|en|Air raids on Japan|WD=Q590545|lt=1945 air raids}} on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''. There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*{{ill|Nasushiobara|en|Nasushiobara|WD=Q498027|lt=Nasushiobara}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture}} *{{ill|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|en|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|WD=Q1197771|lt=Fushimi-ku, Kyoto}} *{{ill|Shimonoseki|en|Shimonoseki|WD=Q203308|lt=Shimonoseki}}, {{ill|Yamaguchi Prefecture|en|Yamaguchi Prefecture|WD=Q127264|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture}} *{{ill|Hannō|en|Hannō|WD=Q850472|lt=Hannō}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture}}
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from {{ill|Nogizaka Station|en|Nogizaka Station|WD=Q347791|lt=Nogizaka Station}} on the {{ill|Tokyo Metro|en|Tokyo Metro|WD=Q682894|lt=Tokyo Metro}} [[:en:Chiyoda Line|Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
==See also==
*{{ill|Tōgō Shrine|en|Tōgō Shrine|WD=Q1384780|lt=Tōgō Shrine}}
==References== {{Reflist}} * {{Official website|http://www.nogijinja.or.jp/}}

The Tokyo Mayor, Baron Yoshio Sakatani, took the initiative to organise the Chūō Nogi Kai (Central Nogi Association) to build a shrine to the couple within their residence.<ref name="pamphlet" /> It is located in {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|WD=Q1490|lt=Tokyo|1=Tokyo}}, {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|WD=Q17|lt=Japan|1=Japan}}.
The shrine compound includes an example of Western architecture constructed during the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}. It is famous as the site where General Nogi and his wife chose to kill themselves after the Meiji Emperor's death.<ref name="pamphlet" /> The shrine was opened soon after this event but was destroyed during the {{ill|Air raids on Japan|en|Air raids on Japan|WD=Q590545|lt=1945 air raids|1=Air raids on Japan}} on May 25, 1945. The present shrine was built in 1962.<ref>Nogi Shrine official homepage, {{cite web |url=https://www.nogijinja.or.jp/history.html|title=由緒 (in Japanese)|accessdate=2019-06-08}}</ref>
There, {{nihongo|Nogi Maresuke|乃木希典, 乃木希典大人之命}} is celebrated as a [[Shinto]] ''[[kami]]''. There are several Nogi Shrines in Japan including the following locations:
*{{ill|Nasushiobara|en|Nasushiobara|WD=Q498027|lt=Nasushiobara|1=Nasushiobara}}, {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|en|Tochigi Prefecture|WD=Q44843|lt=Tochigi Prefecture|1=Tochigi Prefecture}} *{{ill|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|en|Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|WD=Q1197771|lt=Fushimi-ku, Kyoto|1=Fushimi-ku, Kyoto}} *{{ill|Shimonoseki|en|Shimonoseki|WD=Q203308|lt=Shimonoseki|1=Shimonoseki}}, {{ill|Yamaguchi Prefecture|en|Yamaguchi Prefecture|WD=Q127264|lt=Yamaguchi Prefecture|1=Yamaguchi Prefecture}} *{{ill|Hannō|en|Hannō|WD=Q850472|lt=Hannō|1=Hannō}}, {{ill|Saitama Prefecture|en|Saitama Prefecture|WD=Q128186|lt=Saitama Prefecture|1=Saitama Prefecture}}
==Address== 8-11-27 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 107-0052
==Access== * a one-minute walk from {{ill|Nogizaka Station|en|Nogizaka Station|WD=Q347791|lt=Nogizaka Station|1=Nogizaka Station}} on the {{ill|Tokyo Metro|en|Tokyo Metro|WD=Q682894|lt=Tokyo Metro|1=Tokyo Metro}} [[:en:Chiyoda Line|Chiyoda Line]] (exit 1)
